question 1 line=23 title="Where does the schema come from?"
  resolved line=25 date="2026-09-19" choice="d" note="a marker skeleton the document names. Neither the template nor a config block. The schema is its own file under `templates/schema/<name>.md`, with a baked-in one per built-in type versioned with the library; a document names it in an optional `schema:` frontmatter field, absent meaning the type's own; the template becomes the golden test against it, and a custom type gets the pair scaffolded by `template override`. Reasoning and the full shape in §3. Raised by Donald on reading ADR-0002 Open Question 5: the template is a rendering artifact, and a schema that lives in it cannot be reached by docz-api, cannot be golden-tested, and is silently loosened by an override."
  option a line=37 recommended=true text="**The resolved template, read through `Markers`.** Zero config, custom types get it for free, and `docz template override` is literally \"edit the schema.\" Presence and nesting come from the template; content rules come from the kind. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=41 recommended=false text="A `regions:` block under each type in `.docz.yaml`, with registry defaults for built-ins — explicit, but a second place to keep in step with the template."
  option c line=44 recommended=false text="Both: the template by default, the config block as an override."
  option d line=45 recommended=false text="Other."
question 2 line=47 title="Marker spelling on the read side"
  resolved line=49 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note=""
  option a line=51 recommended=true text="**Lenient read, canonical write, spelling reported as a warning and fixed by the migration pass.** The INV-0009 lesson applied to the new markers on day one. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=54 recommended=false text="Canonical spelling only; a variant is not a marker and validate reports the resulting missing region."
  option c line=56 recommended=false text="Other."
question 3 line=58 title="Is the finding message part of the contract?"
  resolved line=60 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note=""
  option a line=62 recommended=true text="**`Code` is the contract; `Detail` is a default a consumer may replace by code.** Linters work this way, docz-api can map codes to its own wording, and the CLI prints `Detail` as-is. R4's \"wording only in L4\" bends here on purpose: a validator with dozens of codes and no default text would force every consumer to write the same table. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=68 recommended=false text="Codes and structured fields only, no `Detail`; `cmd/` owns a wording table."
  option c line=70 recommended=false text="Other."
question 4 line=72 title="How is the corpus migrated?"
  resolved line=74 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note="Amended 2026-09-20: (c). Once inference became a permanent fallback rather than a one-shot heuristic (§6), the pass is defined by findings — `region.inferred` and `marker.spelling` — and belongs to the command that reports them: `docz validate --fix` writes the markers inference found, re-validates, and prints what remains. \"Fix\" promises exactly that and nothing more. Plain `validate` is the preview, so there is no dry-run flag, and no `update --regions`."
  option a line=82 recommended=true text="**`docz update --regions`, dry-run aware, one-shot by nature.** No new command family for a pass each repo runs once; the flag can be removed in a later major without anyone noticing. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=85 recommended=false text="`docz migrate regions` — clearer name, one more command family."
  option c line=86 recommended=false text="`docz validate --fix` — but the fixer only inserts and canonicalizes markers, and \"fix\" promises more."
  option d line=88 recommended=false text="Other."
question 5 line=90 title="Do ToC and index drift belong to validate?"
  resolved line=92 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note="Issue #97's `update --check` is subsumed; the issue was retargeted at `docz validate` on 2026-09-20 (title, body note, and comment) and closes when IMPL-0018 Phase 5 lands. v1 never gets `--check`."
  option a line=97 recommended=true text="**Yes.** A stale ToC is a document finding (`toc.stale`) and a stale README is a repository finding; `docz validate` therefore subsumes issue #97's `update --check` and the CI story is one command. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=101 recommended=false text="Keep drift in `update --check` as #97 proposes and let validate check documents only."
  option c line=103 recommended=false text="Other."
question 6 line=105 title="Which regions does the IMPL template mark?"
  resolved line=107 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note=""
  option a line=109 recommended=true text="**The full set: `phase` with nested `tasks` and `criteria`, plus `testing` and `references`.** Fifteen pairs on a five-phase document is the cost; the spans a program needs are all explicit and the testing exclusion stops being a heading-text rule. *(recommendation, per review)*"
  option b line=113 recommended=false text="`phase` only, with `tasks` and `criteria` still found by heading inside the region — fewer markers, one heuristic kept."
  option c line=115 recommended=false text="Other."
question 7 line=117 title="Hand-rolled walker or a CommonMark AST?"
  resolved line=119 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note=""
  option a line=121 recommended=true text="**Hand-rolled, stdlib-only, matching the other `docparse` walkers.** Marker lines are trivially recognized at the line level; the public core stays stdlib plus yaml; the frozen fence rule is reused. Trigger for revisiting: if CommonMark-fidelity bugs like #96 keep arriving, migrate the walkers onto goldmark *behind* the frozen `docparse` contract with parity goldens, the way `toc` was moved onto `docparse`. The markers are unaffected either way. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=128 recommended=false text="Adopt goldmark now for all of `docparse`, with a docz extension that parses markers into AST nodes."
  option c line=130 recommended=false text="Other."
question 8 line=132 title="Unknown kinds"
  resolved line=134 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note=""
  option a line=136 recommended=true text="**Allowed; well-formedness only.** A custom type's template can declare `<!--docz:risks:start-->` and validate checks pairing, nesting, and presence but no content rule. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=139 recommended=false text="Warn on kinds outside the catalogue."
  option c line=140 recommended=false text="Other."
question 9 line=142 title="Should the ToC and index splices sit on the region walker?"
  resolved line=148 date="2026-09-19" choice="a" note="§1's index-marker rule and §2's catalogue are definitive; DESIGN-0014 §2.5 and §2.6 record the internal change to `toc` and `index`."
  option a line=152 recommended=true text="**Internally yes, externally nothing changes.** `Regions` reports `<!--toc:start-->` as kind `toc` and the README `DOCZ AUTO-GENERATED` pair as kind `index`, both under their legacy spellings; `toc.UpdateToC` and `index.Splice` locate their span through it. One marker walker module-wide, and validate's `toc.stale` check reads the same span the splicer writes. The frozen `toc` behaviour stays pinned by its golden. *(recommendation)*"
  option b line=159 recommended=false text="Leave both splices alone; `Regions` reports `toc` for validation only and never sees the index pair."
  option c line=161 recommended=false text="Other."
